english.title: Purchase / acquire / sell / transport a specimen of unlawfully imported / acquired species listed in Annex B

english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used for acts carried out after 30th September 2018; the Control of Trade in Endangered Species (Enforcement) Regulations 1997 are revoked by the Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/703) from 1st October 2018.
(ii) Regulation 8(4) of the Control of Trade in Endangered Species (Enforcement) Regulations 1997 provides that a person shall not be guilty of an offence under this paragraph if he proves that at the time the alleged offence was committed he had no reason to believe that the specimen was a specimen of a species listed in Annex B.
(iii) Regulation 8(5) of the Control of Trade in Endangered Species (Enforcement) Regulations 1997 provides that a person shall not be guilty of an offence under this paragraph if he proves:-
(a) that at the time when the specimen first came into his possession he made such enquiries (if any) as in the circumstances were reasonable in order to ascertain whether it was imported or acquired unlawfully; and (b) that at the time the alleged offence was committed, he had no reason to believe that the specimen was imported or acquired unlawfully.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
